thread:
priya: Quick sync — proposing we consolidate the several cloud marketplace ref-arch repos into a single "starter-kit" umbrella. One repo, multiple provider modules, consistent Terraform patterns. Goal: faster partner enablement and fewer support gaps. Thoughts?

devon: +1 from eng-templates. Main concerns: module interface parity (inputs/outputs) and CI matrices for aws/azure/gcp.

kevin: Agree. Also need to ensure marketplace packaging requirements per cloud (licenses, metadata). Can we make a packaging pipeline that emits provider-specific artifacts?

elaine: From partnerships POV we want one-click deploy examples for partners and an opinionated network layout for compliance customers. Also want clear docs for pricing/instance sizing guidance (e.g., GPU SKUs).

priya: High level plan I had in mind: 1) repo layout + naming convention 2) common module spec (variables + outputs) 3) smoke tests + e2e matrix 4) publishing pipeline (provider artifacts + marketplace metadata) 5) partner docs + example stacks.

devon: For common module spec, propose minimal required set: `name`, `region`, `instance_type`, `node_count`, `network_subnet_id`, `tags`. Outputs should include `lb_dns`, `instance_ids`, `module_version`. Keep everything optional where feasible with sane defaults.

kevin: For packaging pipeline we can do a GitHub Actions workflow that builds provider artifacts and pushes to a release. Also one job to generate marketplace metadata JSON. I can draft a workflow.

elaine: Can we include a short partner onboarding checklist in the repo root, like `ONBOARDING.md` — items: security review, sample deployment, billing SKU guidance, support contact. That helps partner success managers.

priya: Yes. Also need a name convention for modules: `redwood/<provider>/refkit/<component>`? open to alternatives.

devon: That works. Suggest we add a versioning policy: semantic for modules, and ephemeral tags for example stacks.

kevin: FYI marketplace requirements vary: Azure wants ARM templates or managed images + listing metadata; GCP wants deployment manager/terraform + marketplace metadata; AWS wants CloudFormation/AMI or SaaS listing. We should maintain a small adapter per provider.

priya: Example usage snippet to include in README:

```
module "refkit_inference" {
  source = "github.com/redwood-inference/refkit-starter//modules/aws/inference"
  name = "refkit-dev"
  region = "us-west-2"
  instance_type = "g4dn.xlarge"
  node_count = 2
}
```

elaine: Nice. Make sure sample has cost caveats + recommended lower-cost config for evaluation (e.g., CPU-only option).

devon: CI matrix plan: terraform fmt/check, terratest smoke (small instance), static analysis (tflint), validate metadata generator. Run matrix across providers and terraform versions. We should gate merges on the matrix passing for the providers the PR touches.

kevin: I'll draft `ci/publish.yml` and `ci/matrix.yml` and link to partner legal for metadata requirements.

opsbot: CI pipeline created: `refkit-starter/ci/matrix` (build triggered). Status: queued.

priya: Timeline proposal: draft RFC + repo skeleton by EOD Friday (owner: devon), CI + packaging draft by next Wed (owner: kevin), partner docs + examples by next Fri (owner: elaine).

elaine: I'm good with that. I'll start assembling the onboarding checklist and sample partner email templates.

devon: I'll open the RFC PR with repository skeleton. Will include a starter `modules/aws`, `modules/azure`, `modules/gcp`, `examples/` and `ci/`.

kevin: Cool — will follow up with a sample GH Actions workflow and metadata generator script.

priya: Awesome. Action items summarized: 
- devon: RFC + repo skeleton (due EOD Fri)
- kevin: CI + packaging draft (due Wed)
- elaine: partner docs + onboarding checklist (due next Fri)
- everyone: review RFC once PR is up, comment inline.

elaine: tagging partners team once RFC is up. @here :thumbsup:

priya: Thanks all — feeling good about this. We'll post a one-pager for the execs once we have the skeleton and CI demo.

devon: PR incoming shortly.

opsbot: CI status: `refkit-starter/ci/matrix` queued -> running.
